overview: Two types of aneuploidy differing in whether a chromosome is missing or duplicated.
genZNote: Monosomy: one chromosome didn't show up. Trisomy: one chromosome brought a plus-one nobody invited.

aspects.label: Chromosome Count
aspects.valueA: One chromosome of a pair is missing (2n-1).
aspects.valueB: One extra chromosome present, making a set of three (2n+1).

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Turner syndrome (45, X — monosomy of X chromosome).
aspects.valueB: Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Klinefelter syndrome (XXY, a trisomy of sex chromosomes).

aspects.label: General Severity
aspects.valueA: Often more severe or lethal, since a whole chromosome's genes are missing.
aspects.valueB: Often somewhat more survivable, since extra genetic material is usually tolerated better than a deficit.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Down syndrome = trisomy 21. Turner syndrome = monosomy X (45,X). Klinefelter = XXY trisomy.
overlay.memoryTrick: Mono = one missing. Tri = one extra.
overlay.commonMisconception: Turner syndrome is monosomy of a sex chromosome, not an autosome — don't mix it up with Down syndrome.
